title: Poems from the Divan of Hafiz
author: hafiz
attributionNote: The attribution is not disputed in the scholarship this catalogue follows.
description: Gertrude Bell's selection from Hafiz's Divan: ghazals of wine, the beloved, the tavern and the garden, in which the erotic and the mystical readings are held together rather than resolved. Bell's introduction reads the poems as the work of a man who kept the pleasure of the world and the hope of something beyond it in the same frame.
historicalContext: Hafiz lived in Shiraz in the fourteenth century. Bell's translations were published in 1897 and were among the first English renderings by a woman of a major Persian poet; they are verse translations of selected ghazals, not the complete Divan.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Project Gutenberg at read time: the whole plain-text edition is fetched and split at the chapter headings it prints. The 1897 translation by Gertrude Lowthian Bell is public domain in the United States.
